yusefi.notes: Registry clerk. Has stamped four thousand of these.

ebadi.notes: Your teacher. Forty children, nine seconds, one decision.

karimi.notes: Conscription desk. Genuinely does not know how long it takes.

sharifi.notes: Your supervisor. Has watched this happen to four students.

omid.notes: Your friend since the bicycle. Jokes about not going back.

nader.notes: Your first employer. Counts the cash twice, politely.

mitra.notes: Pharmacist. Explains the banking system to people in pain.

shirin.notes: Bank teller abroad. Breaks a rule to help you, quietly.

hosseini.notes: Consular clerk. The monitor turns, the answer does not.

doyle.notes: US screening officer. Says 'random' on every flight.

system.notes: Automated text: emails, signs, recorded announcements.

SC-HOME-NIGHT.note: A room with one window and a paraffin heater. Where you are born, and where the offer letter is read years later.

SC-HOME-DAY.note: The same room in daylight. Reused deliberately: the journey returns to one room and it is never different.

SC-COURTYARD.note: Walled courtyard, a tree, fruit. The only scene in the set with nothing to lose.

SC-STREET-DAY.note: The four streets a bicycle makes reachable, and the junction at the end of them.

SC-CLASSROOM.note: Forty children, one decision made in nine seconds.

SC-EXAM-HALL.note: The konkur. Rows and rows of the same desk.

SC-BARRACKS.note: Where the card is issued, which is not about the army.

SC-CAMPUS.note: A list taped to a wall. Later, the same wall, and the name on the certificate is now a flag.

SC-OFFICE.note: Cash in an envelope, counted twice because that is polite.

SC-AIRPORT.note: Departures. Used for the easy trip and, much later, for the visit that never happens.

SC-AIRPORT-SEC.note: The side of the hall the four letters send you to.

SC-CONSULATE.note: A counter, a window, and a queue that starts outside. Used for both the Turkish registration and the passport surrender.

SC-REGISTRY.note: Where your name is written down one letter wrong, permanently.

SC-BANK.note: A compliance decision arriving at a counter staffed by somebody who did not make it.

SC-DESK-NIGHT.note: Two sentences in an email, read at a desk at night.

SC-PEARSON.note: US preclearance at Toronto Pearson. Standing in Canada, at a counter that is legally the United States. The boss arena; dressed but not yet used.

start.text: You are born in a room with a paraffin heater and one window.
You will not remember any of this. It happens anyway.
He's here. He's small, but he's here.
You survive the first year, which is the only achievement that will never appear on any document you are asked for later.
Mansour has been thinking about your name for four months. It means something. He is pleased with it.
It's from the poem. The one about the road.
Spell it.
Your father spells it. Mr Yusefi writes without looking up, and stamps the page.

options.text: Ask to see what he wrote

check.text: It is not correct. It is one letter different, and Mr Yusefi is not reprinting a certificate over one letter.

leave.text: Nobody reads it closely for nineteen years.

out.text: The spelling on this page is now the spelling of your name, in every system that will ever ask for it.

start.text: Farideh opens it with her thumbs rather than a knife, because a knife bruises the seeds.
Hold your hands out. No - flat.
Good. Now don't move, {player}.
You eat pomegranate in the courtyard until your fingers stain.
Nothing follows from this. It triggers nothing, costs nothing, and cannot be taken away from you later.

a-bicycle-and-the-junction.title: A bicycle, and the range it gives you

start.text: Second-hand, the wrong size, and it doubles the size of the world in an afternoon.
Not past the main road, {player}.

options.text: Stay this side of the road
Go and look at the main road

obey.text: You ride the same four streets until you know every crack in them.

further.text: You go as far as the junction and stop, because the noise is enormous.
You will remember this as the first time you understood that somewhere else existed.

the-teacher-who-decided.title: The teacher who decided you were clever

start.text: Mrs Ebadi has forty children and has decided something about you on the evidence of one answer.
{player}. Stay behind a minute.
You're going to sit the exam. Not that one. The other one.
It is the most consequential thing anyone does for you, and she does it in about nine seconds.

the-konkur.title: Passing the exam that decides the next ten years

start.text: The konkur. Six hundred thousand people sitting the same paper on the same morning, for a number of places that is not six hundred thousand.
You pass. Your rank is good - specifically, good enough for a university whose name will later be the problem.
Two years. You knew about the two years.
Card.
What you did not know is that the card is not about the army. The card is about the passport.
No card, no exit permit. No exit permit, nothing.

options.text: Ask how long it takes after service

options.note: not the man to argue with

ask.text: He is not being obstructive. He genuinely does not know, it genuinely varies, and nobody above him will say either.

quiet.text: He hands it back and moves on to the next one.

out.text: Every plan you make for the next two years has this in front of it.

the-list-taped-to-the-wall.title: Getting into the place you did not expect

start.text: The list is printed and taped to a wall and your name is on it.
Sharif. You got Sharif, {player}.
Roya cries in a way you have not seen before. Mansour telephones people who do not care.
Four years later. Same name, same certificate.
You should know it's on a list now, {player}.
Not you. The university.
The thing that made your mother cry is now the line on your CV that makes an export-control officer stop reading.

options.note: more than one, which is the problem

options.text: Ask whether it can be appealed

which.text: Depends whose. That's rather the difficulty.

appeal.text: By whom? You aren't the one listed. The building is.

out.text: You finish it. It is a good degree. It is now also a flag.

first-pay-in-an-envelope.title: The first pay for work you did yourself

start.text: Cash, in an envelope, counted twice in front of you because that is polite.
Don't spend it on nothing, {player}. Spend it on something.
You buy Roya something she would not buy herself, keep the rest, and feel enormous.
Everybody goes to Istanbul. It is the one place that does not require asking permission first.
You are twenty-four, you are in another country, and the ferry costs almost nothing.
We could just not go back on Sunday, {player}.

options.text: Say nothing, and think about it

consider.text: You go back on Sunday, and think about it the whole flight.

out.text: You have now been abroad. It was easy. This will turn out to be misleading.

the-province-is-closed.title: The address decides, and the address is closed

start.text: The second visit to Turkey is not a holiday. You are trying to live there, legally, with paperwork.
Which province is the address in?
You tell him. He turns his monitor slightly, the way people do before saying something they did not decide.
That province is closed to new registrations.

options.note: the list moves; that is the design

out.text: The flat exists. The lease exists. The address is the wrong address, and no version of you could have known.

start.text: The offer letter is a PDF and you read it eleven times.
Funded. Actually funded, not funded-in-principle.
Then you're going.
Between this document and that country there are four other documents, and you do not yet know what any of them cost.
The clearance is a form about your subject, not about you. You fill it in honestly, because there is no other way to fill it in.
Eleven weeks later there is an email with two sentences in it.
Your application has not been successful. No further information can be provided.

reply.text: The reply is automatic and repeats the second sentence.

reapply.text: You lose a term. The answer is the same.

uni.text: We can ask. We've asked before.

out.text: Your subject is the reason, and nobody will say so in writing, because saying so in writing is exactly what they are avoiding.

the-account-closed-by-nobody.title: The account closed in a country you are not at war with

start.text: The letter is a month old by the time you see it. The account closes in fourteen days.
It's a compliance decision. I can't see the reason.
Nobody here can, honestly. It comes from somewhere else.

options.text: Ask to speak to that somewhere else
Ask what happens to the money
Ask if another bank will take you

escalate.text: There isn't a number. I've looked, for other people.

money.text: You can withdraw it. Bring ID. Bring all of it.

other.text: Try a smaller one. Don't mention this one.
She has broken a rule to tell you that, and she knows it, and she does it anyway.

out.text: You are not accused of anything. There is nothing to appeal, because nothing was decided about you specifically.

surrender-the-only-passport.title: You must surrender your only passport to renew it

start.text: To renew it you post it away. There is one of it. There is no second one, and no receipt that functions as one.
Six to eight weeks. Sometimes more.

options.text: Ask what you travel on meanwhile

hand.text: You put your identity in a padded envelope and watch someone put it in a tray with other people's.
For two months you are, for every practical purpose, unable to prove you are anyone.

medicine-that-cannot-be-paid-for.title: A war with no explosion and the same casualties

start.text: It is not banned. That is the sentence everyone repeats. Medicine is not sanctioned.
It's not the drug. It's the payment.
No bank will touch the transfer, so the importer stopped importing.

options.note: there is one, and it is worse

sub.text: There's an alternative. It's older. She'll feel it.

others.text: Which requires someone who can travel.

out.text: Nothing was aimed at Roya. She is simply downstream of a decision about a banking system.

start.text: You have a life here now. It is a small life and it is yours.
They apply twice. Both times the refusal is the same subsection, and the subsection is about whether they intend to go home.
They think we want to stay.
Why would we want to stay, {player}? Everything we have is here.

options.note: you will; it will not work

again.text: You apply again in the spring. The subsection does not change.

silence.text: You tell her the weather is bad here anyway. She lets you.

out.text: Your daughter will meet her grandmother on a screen, held at the wrong angle, for eleven years.

start.text: Four letters printed on the boarding pass, where other people's say nothing at all.
Step out of the line, sir. Random check.
It has been random on every flight for six years.

argue.text: Sir. Step out of the line.
The tone changes on the second sentence. You learn not to have the first conversation again.

comply.text: You take your shoes off before being asked, because it is faster, and because you have done this before.

out.text: You are not stopped from flying. You are simply never not stopped.

start.text: US preclearance, Toronto Pearson. You are standing in Canada. The booth is the United States. That distinction will matter shortly.
One officer is taking the whole line today. The board says his name but you cannot read it from here.
Ahead of you a Korean man in a good coat has been at the counter eleven minutes and has begun to repeat himself.

options.note: they are correct; not the variable

watch.text: The officer is not shouting. He is asking the same question in four different shapes and writing down each answer.

check.text: Everything is in order. Everything has been in order every time.

out.text: The Korean man picks up his folder, walks back past the line, and does not look at anyone.
[The Iranian run ends here. Officer Choi is a later task.]
